supersedes: All earlier multi-period figures before cumulative payout correction.
caveats: Wasserstein risk bounds use an explicit max_path transport metric on normalized path prices and cumulative payout requirements, unrestricted support and a development-selected radius, not a confidence-calibrated ambiguity set. Utility remains nominal.

Final all-risk verdict uses separate Bonferroni-adjusted one-sided conditional batch bounds for every payment, path/terminal loss and holdings. Reference, nominal and stress measures plus their common-threshold convex-hull envelope are checked. These are Monte Carlo diagnostics, not economic forecast coverage. Zero observed losses do not bound unseen tails.
Funding-selected candidates remain frozen when final all-risk evaluation fails. Final results never tune or repair them. Passing a coarse model check is not an investment recommendation.
Archive split independence is the input provider responsibility; generated mode uses disjoint calibration/evaluation seeds. Final failures are never recalibrated away.
Stressed posterior and nominal share funding/CML thresholds, covering their finite convex hull only.
Liabilities, views and innovation-law parameters are illustrative/development-selected, not client evidence. Scenario law: gaussian_scale_mixture

Weekly log shocks aggregate by summation. Read innovation_evidence for the selected iid, conditional or legacy model domain. Legacy t cannot support population price means/variances; iid exact formulas do not apply to recursive conditional variance.
Cumulative payouts use money-market opportunity costs, not dynamic rebalancing. RE uses an explicit fixed planned sale/settlement schedule; marked value is not available cash.
Cash mixing is an explicit validation-selected portfolio calibration grid, not a claim of globally optimal robust weights.
1/N allocates the free budget equally subject to floors and fixed initial holdings; all allocation comparators and the displayed frontier honor those holdings.

qualifications: Illustrative, not client-calibrated. All dollar amounts are USD.

Displayed return and volatility describe finite simulated paths, not economic forecasts. Explicit legacy log-Student-t modes do not have finite population price moments. The new Gaussian-mixture default does. Certainty equivalent is risk-adjusted net wealth, not expected profit.
CML is a tail average of loss from initial capital before payouts, not peak-to-trough maximum drawdown. Observed maximum loss is not a guaranteed limit.

The fan is marked wealth, not available cash, after cumulative payouts and configured synthetic liquidity haircuts, with money-market opportunity costs. RE follows an explicit fixed sale/settlement plan, not a dynamic asset-sale policy.
Stress cards are deterministic simplified shocks, not calibrated historical crisis replays or probability forecasts.
Time-to-cash has not been calibrated. A liquid-market label does not guarantee same-day sale or settlement.
Wasserstein risk bounds use a development radius and explicit unrestricted-support transport metric; utility is nominal. No probability coverage is guaranteed by the radius.
Zero observed losses is not a bound on unseen tails.

calibration.history_note: Public Singapore URA quarterly price-index returns, annualized with4 periods/year; four-quarter circular block bootstrap. calibration.forward_note: 4% default is an illustrative long-run price-log-return view, not a data estimate, calibrated prior, conservative bound or promised return. Net rent is separate.
